title: Staged memory eviction, partial KV spill, and model-fallback retry policy for GPU OOM recovery
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:

As model context lengths and concurrent request volumes increase, we hit GPU OOMs despite existing continuous-batching and KV cache heuristics. Current failures either fail the request outright or force a full model fallback (cold CPU) which has long tail latency and poor user experience. We need a graded, low-latency recovery path that preserves as much correctness as possible while avoiding hard failures and expensive fallbacks.

Goal:

Design and implement a staged OOM prevention and recovery policy combining: (1) proactive partial KV spill to host-pinned memory, (2) per-layer/segment eviction with prioritized restoration, (3) token-length graceful degradation (truncation/backpressure), and (4) deterministic model-downgrade + retry policy (quantized variant or narrower model) before falling back to CPU. The policy should be configurable per-customer and observable in the Console.

Success criteria:

- Reduce hard OOM request failures by >= 90% under synthetic high-concurrency tests (same cluster config).
- Median extra latency added by recovery path <= 25 ms for GPU-resident recoveries (partial spill + staged retry).
- Fall-back to smaller/quantized model increases latency by X but is used < 5% of incidents in baseline traffic.
- Telemetry: new metrics emitted for recovery path counts, average spill size, eviction frequency, and per-request degradation phases.

Design proposal (high level):

1) Proactive memory guardrail and allocation staging
- Add a pre-allocation probe for large KV cache growth requests. If free GPU memory < threshold (configurable per device/class), mark request as "at-risk" and enter staged recovery pipeline instead of attempting full allocation.

2) Partial KV spill and pinned host staging
- Evict oldest low-priority KV segments (configurable per-model) and write to pinned host memory region (mlock/pinned pages) so we can restore without device-to-host page faults thrashing. Spilled segments are compressed (fast LZ4) where beneficial.
- Keep a lightweight index in GPU memory for spilled segments so we can progressively restore high-priority segments first (recent tokens, high-attention heads).

3) Layer/segment prioritized eviction
- Define priority buckets per-layer and per-KV-slice (e.g., recent N tokens high priority, older tokens low). Evict from low priority first. Eviction is incremental to avoid long pauses.

4) Graceful request-level degradation
- If eviction and spill cannot free enough memory, perform deterministic response degradation: reduce generation max_tokens for the in-flight request, remove top-k sampling expansion, or apply prefix-dropping heuristics for very long prompts. Policy is configured per-route.

5) Staged retry with model downgrade
- After spill+eviction+degrade fail, retry on the same GPU with a quantized model variant (e.g., 4-bit) or a smaller architectural variant pinned on the node. This retry path is instrumented and bounded (max retries = 2, exponential jitter).
- Only if quantized/smaller variants are not compatible or capacity-constrained, fallback to CPU-hosted model as last resort.

6) Safety and isolation
- Enforce per-tenant memory accounting; prevent recovery for one tenant from evicting critical segments of others. Recovery must adhere to per-deployment memory safety budgets.

Rollout plan:

Phase 0: Simulation and testing (this ticket)
- Implement a simulator that replays production trace (from console traces) to model KV growth and memory pressure. Use different parameter sweeps for thresholds, spill compression, and eviction strategies.
- Create fault-injection harness that triggers probe failures and measures recovery latency.

Phase 1: Canary on low-traffic pools
- Deploy spill+evict read-only (no automatic retry) to collect metrics and validate restoration correctness.
- Then enable staged retry with model-downgrade for a small % of requests.

Phase 2: Gradual rollout and policy tuning
- Increase coverage, tune thresholds per GPU SKU, and add Console controls for tenant operators.

Phase 3: Full rollout and deprecation of cold CPU fallback for recoverable cases

Testing and metrics:

- Unit tests for spill/restore correctness across model architectures and KV shapes.
- Integration tests with continuous-batching to validate no deadlock between batching aggregator and eviction thread.
- Load tests: replay of synthetic spike + long-context sessions.
- Metrics to emit: recovery_attempts_total, recovery_success_total, spill_bytes_total, average_restore_latency_ms, per-request-degradation_phase (none|spill|evict|degrade|downgrade|cpu-fallback).

Security and compliance:

- Spilled KV in host memory must respect encryption at rest when required by tenant configuration. Use KMS-managed keys where enabled. Ensure pinned pages cannot be swapped to disk or captured by other processes.

Open questions:

- Threshold calibration: static thresholds vs dynamic learned thresholds based on traffic patterns.
- Compression trade-offs: CPU cost vs reduced transfer time for large spills.
- Interaction with continuous-batching: When to pause batching aggregation to prioritize low-latency restoration?

comments: 2025-02-13: Initial write-up and simulator prototype created. Aisha: added baseline metrics and success criteria.
2025-02-14: Engineering sync — agreed to try pinned host memory for spilled segments; Marco to prototype spill format (LZ4 vs none).
2025-02-17: Design review with Runtime and Serving teams. Action: add per-tenant memory budgets and encryption requirements. Assigned to security review.
2025-02-19: Prototype results: partial spills avoid OOM in 78% of synthetic stress runs. Restore latency median 18ms, 95th 140ms. Need to reduce 95th by improving compression pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: No hard OOMs in canary pool for 7 consecutive days under replicated production traces
Telemetry for recovery phases emitted and visible in Console dashboard
Automated tests for spill/restore across CPU/GPU and quantized variants added to CI
Policy controls exposed in Console for tenant override
implementation_notes: Add a memory-probe API in allocator: try_reserve(bytes) -> {ok|at-risk|fail}
Implement pinned host spill store with LZ4 compression and fixed-size chunking
Maintain an in-GPU index of spilled chunks with priority metadata for progressive restore
Expose per-route recovery policy flags (enable_spill, enable_degrade, allowed_downgrades)
Integrate with existing batching scheduler to preempt large batch builds when a request is in recovery state
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Spilling too aggressively increases host memory pressure and CPU load. Mitigation: rate-limit spills per-node and add backpressure signals to scheduler.
Risk: Incorrect restore order can degrade quality. Mitigation: prioritize most-recent and high-attention heads, validate with eval sets.
Risk: Latency spikes on restore. Mitigation: incremental restore and parallel DMA when supported by driver.
Risk: Cross-tenant impact. Mitigation: strict tenant budgets and auditor for spill operations.
